edges.description: Reduced functional ABCA1 lowers apolipoprotein A-I-mediated export of cellular cholesterol and phospholipid.
edges.target: Reduced Cellular Cholesterol and Phospholipid Efflux

edges.description: Less cholesterol and phospholipid is transferred to lipid-poor apoA-I, limiting formation and maturation of HDL particles.
edges.source: Reduced Cellular Cholesterol and Phospholipid Efflux

edges.description: ABCA1-deficient macrophages show increased inflammatory gene expression; carriers have raised arterial FDG uptake and circulating cytokines.
edges.source: Reduced Cellular Cholesterol and Phospholipid Efflux

edges.description: Lower apoA-I- and HDL-mediated efflux is associated with greater carotid intima-media thickness among ABCA1 mutation carriers.
edges.source: Reduced Cellular Cholesterol and Phospholipid Efflux
edges.target: Increased carotid artery intimal medial thickness

edges.description: In family-based cohorts, carriers with lower residual efflux more often have coronary artery disease.
edges.source: Reduced Cellular Cholesterol and Phospholipid Efflux

edges.description: Reduced HDL formation lowers plasma HDL cholesterol in proportion to the residual efflux.
Fewer mature HDL particles and faster clearance of poorly lipidated apoA-I lower plasma apoA-I.
A proinflammatory effect of ABCA1 deficiency is proposed to contribute to atherogenesis; this rests on mouse data and has not been shown to mediate coronary disease in human carriers.

edges.source: LDL-Lowering and Non-HDL Risk Factor Management

evidence.reference_title: Mutations in ABC1 in Tangier disease and familial high-density lipoprotein deficiency.
evidence.snippet: Mutations in ABC1 were detected in both TD and FHA, indicating that TD and FHA are allelic.

evidence.reference_title: Mutations in the ABC1 gene in familial HDL deficiency with defective cholesterol efflux.
evidence.snippet: These data show that mutations in ABC1 are the major cause of familial HDL deficiency associated with defective cholesterol efflux, and that CERP has an essential role in the formation of HDL.

nodes.description: A heterozygous germline ABCA1 variant (missense, nonsense, frameshift or splice) reduces the amount or activity of the ATP-binding cassette transporter that loads lipid-poor apolipoprotein A-I with cellular phospholipid and cholesterol. Missense variants differ in how severely they impair trafficking, apoA-I binding and efflux, and that severity tracks the lipid phenotype.

evidence.reference_title: Mutations in ABC1 in Tangier disease and familial high-density lipoprotein deficiency.
evidence.snippet: Mutations in ABC1 were detected in both TD and FHA, indicating that TD and FHA are allelic.

evidence.reference_title: Mutations in the ABC1 gene in familial HDL deficiency with defective cholesterol efflux.
evidence.snippet: These data show that mutations in ABC1 are the major cause of familial HDL deficiency associated with defective cholesterol efflux, and that CERP has an essential role in the formation of HDL.

evidence.reference_title: ABCA1(Alabama): a novel variant associated with HDL deficiency and premature coronary artery disease.
evidence.snippet: These data confirm recent data that a single defective allele in ABCA1 may be associated with reduced HDL cholesterol and FHA.

evidence.reference_title: Specific mutations in ABCA1 have discrete effects on ABCA1 function and lipid phenotypes both in vivo and in vitro.
evidence.snippet: we determined that the phenotypes of patients correlate with the severity and nature of defects in ABCA1 function.

evidence.reference_title: Functional characterization of missense variants affecting the extracellular domains of ABCA1 using a fluorescence-based assay.
evidence.snippet: Among these, only 12 variants showed a distinct loss-of-function phenotype, asserting their direct association with severe HDL disorders.

genetic_context.description: One pathogenic allele with the other allele intact; biallelic loss causes Tangier disease instead.

nodes.description: Heterozygous carriers show raised arterial 18F-FDG uptake and increased circulating TNF-alpha, MCP-1 and IL-6, with increased TNF-alpha mRNA in monocytes, consistent with a proinflammatory state that may contribute to atherogenesis. Statin users among carriers had lower arterial FDG uptake.

evidence.reference_title: Increased Systemic and Plaque Inflammation in ABCA1 Mutation Carriers With Attenuation by Statins.
evidence.snippet: Heterozygous ABCA1 mutation carriers had a 20% higher target:background ratio than in controls (target:background ratio; P=0.008).

evidence.reference_title: Increased Systemic and Plaque Inflammation in ABCA1 Mutation Carriers With Attenuation by Statins.
evidence.snippet: Only TNFα mRNA was increased in monocytes from heterozygous ABCA1 mutation carriers.

nodes.description: Plasma HDL cholesterol is typically about half of normal and often below the fifth percentile for age and sex. Age modifies the phenotype in heterozygotes, and not every carrier falls below population thresholds.

evidence.reference_title: Age and residual cholesterol efflux affect HDL cholesterol levels and coronary artery disease in ABCA1 heterozygotes.
evidence.snippet: ABCA1 heterozygotes have decreased HDL cholesterol (HDL-C) and increased triglycerides.

evidence.reference_title: Age and residual cholesterol efflux affect HDL cholesterol levels and coronary artery disease in ABCA1 heterozygotes.
evidence.snippet: Age is an important modifier of the phenotype in heterozygotes

evidence.reference_title: Cellular cholesterol transport and efflux in fibroblasts are abnormal in subjects with familial HDL deficiency.
evidence.snippet: characterized by a severe decrease in the plasma HDL cholesterol (-C) level (less than the fifth percentile)

evidence.reference_title: Tangier disease caused by compound heterozygosity for ABCA1 mutations R282X and Y1532C.
evidence.snippet: Relatives who were heterozygous for one of these mutations, had about half-normal HDL cholesterol levels.

evidence.reference_title: Association of loss-of-function mutations in the ABCA1 gene with high-density lipoprotein cholesterol levels and risk of ischemic heart disease.
evidence.snippet: corresponding to a reduction in HDL cholesterol of 17 mg/dL (P < .001)

evidence.reference_title: Familial HDL deficiency due to ABCA1 gene mutations with or without other genetic lipoprotein disorders.
evidence.snippet: Plasma HDL-C and Apo A-I values in these subjects were 38.3 and 36.9% lower than in unaffected family members

nodes.description: Poorly lipidated apoA-I forms fewer mature particles: carriers are depleted of large alpha- and pre-alpha-migrating HDL while small pre-beta-1 HDL is preserved, and poorly lipidated apoA-I is cleared faster from plasma.

evidence.reference_title: High-density lipoprotein subpopulations in pathologic conditions.
evidence.snippet: Tangier heterozygotes are severely depleted in the larger alpha- and pre-alpha-mobility subspecies.

evidence.reference_title: Diagnosis and treatment of high density lipoprotein deficiency.
evidence.snippet: heterozygotes had a lack of large α-1 and α-2 HDL particles, normal preβ-1 HDL, and only 50% of normal cellular cholesterol efflux

nodes.description: Carriers reach the upper limit of normal carotid intima-media thickness about 25 years earlier than controls.
nodes.id: Increased carotid artery intimal medial thickness

evidence.reference_title: Association between increased arterial-wall thickness and impairment in ABCA1-driven cholesterol efflux: an observational study.
evidence.snippet: An intima-media thickness at the upper limit of normal (0.80 mm) was reached by age 55 years in the ABCA1 heterozygotes, and at age 80 years in unaffected controls (p<0.0001).

nodes.description: No therapy corrects the ABCA1 defect. Management is directed at non-HDL cardiovascular risk factors, with statin-based LDL cholesterol lowering where indicated, rather than at raising HDL cholesterol. In a small observational comparison, carriers taking statins had lower arterial wall inflammation than carriers not taking statins.
nodes.id: LDL-Lowering and Non-HDL Risk Factor Management

evidence.reference_title: Diagnosis and treatment of high density lipoprotein deficiency.
evidence.snippet: Treatment should be directed at optimizing all non-HDL risk factors.

nodes.description: Four loss-of-function ABCA1 variants carried heterozygously in the Danish general population, used to test whether genetically lowered HDL cholesterol raises ischemic heart disease risk.

evidence.reference_title: Association of loss-of-function mutations in the ABCA1 gene with high-density lipoprotein cholesterol levels and risk of ischemic heart disease.
evidence.snippet: Heterozygotes vs noncarriers for 4 ABCA1 mutations (P1065S, G1216V, N1800H, R2144X) had HDL cholesterol levels of 41 mg/dL

nodes.description: ABCA1(Alabama), c.254C>T p.Pro85Leu, a heterozygous missense variant that segregated with low HDL cholesterol in a kindred with premature coronary artery disease and was absent from over 400 control chromosomes.

evidence.reference_title: ABCA1(Alabama): a novel variant associated with HDL deficiency and premature coronary artery disease.
evidence.snippet: The proband and affected individuals were heterozygotes for C254T with proline converted to leucine (P85L).

nodes.description: Family-based cohorts report coronary artery disease more often and at an earlier age in heterozygous carriers, concentrated among those with the lowest HDL cholesterol or residual efflux. A Danish general-population study of 109 heterozygotes for four loss-of-function variants found no increased ischemic heart disease, so penetrance is incomplete and the magnitude of risk is unsettled.

evidence.reference_title: Age and residual cholesterol efflux affect HDL cholesterol levels and coronary artery disease in ABCA1 heterozygotes.
evidence.snippet: ABCA1 heterozygotes display a greater than threefold increase in the frequency of coronary artery disease (CAD), with earlier onset than unaffected family members.

evidence.reference_title: Genetic and secondary causes of severe HDL deficiency and cardiovascular disease.
evidence.snippet: Atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) prevalence rates in the ABCA1, LCAT, APOA1, LPL, and mutation-negative groups were 37.0%, 4.0%, 40.0%, 11.1%, and 6.4%, respectively.

evidence.reference_title: Association of loss-of-function mutations in the ABCA1 gene with high-density lipoprotein cholesterol levels and risk of ischemic heart disease.
evidence.snippet: Lower plasma levels of HDL cholesterol due to heterozygosity for loss-of-function mutations in ABCA1 were not associated with an increased risk of IHD.

nodes.description: ApoA-I-mediated cholesterol and phosphatidylcholine efflux is reduced to roughly half of normal in carrier cells (fibroblasts, macrophages), a partial defect compared with the near-absent efflux of Tangier disease. Residual efflux correlates with HDL cholesterol and with arterial-wall measures across carriers.
nodes.id: Reduced Cellular Cholesterol and Phospholipid Efflux

evidence.reference_title: Cellular cholesterol transport and efflux in fibroblasts are abnormal in subjects with familial HDL deficiency.
evidence.snippet: FHD cells displayed an approximately 25% reduction in HDL3-mediated cellular cholesterol efflux and an approximately 50% to 80% reduction in apoA-I-mediated cholesterol and phosphatidylcholine efflux compared with normal cells.

evidence.reference_title: Diagnosis and treatment of high density lipoprotein deficiency.
evidence.snippet: heterozygotes had a lack of large α-1 and α-2 HDL particles, normal preβ-1 HDL, and only 50% of normal cellular cholesterol efflux
